Four frontier models. One week. The AI landscape just shifted.

GPT-6 Astra launched September 3 with no published price. Claude Fable 5.1 arrived on AWS. Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash at $0.75 per million input tokens. And Meta dropped Muse Spark 1.3 at roughly $0.10 per million tokens — making it the cheapest model in the top five on the leaderboard.

The release cadence of major AI models has roughly quadrupled since 2023. That is not hype. That is a verified structural shift in how fast the frontier moves.

For business leaders, three things matter now. Model switching costs are the new vendor lock-in. Inference pricing is collapsing toward commodity levels. And the real value is migrating from the model layer to the orchestration and application layer above it.

The winning strategy is not picking the right model. It is building an architecture that absorbs the next one without a re-engineering cycle.
